tools.description: Executes server-side JavaScript the way Scripts - Background does. Use for complex GlideRecord operations the CRUD tools cannot express. By default (wait: true) the script is POSTed once to the instance's /sys.scripts.do processor as the authenticated user, and the response is parsed into success/failure, output lines, errors, the scope it ran in, and links to its Script Execution History and rollback context. Requires the admin role. A rollback context is recorded by default (record_for_rollback), so the run's record changes can be rolled back from that context. The processor runs in the authenticated user's own session, so that user's current update set is expected to capture tracked configuration writes, and `scope` picks the application scope. The script request is never retried: a timeout, 5xx, or dropped connection is reported as an unknown outcome (check Script Execution History; do not re-run blindly). Only when the processor provably did not run the script (HTTP 401/403/404, a login page, or a connection error before sending) does it fall back to a sys_trigger job, and the response says so. The sys_trigger path (that fallback, or wait: false) runs in the scheduler's own session, not the caller's: tracked configuration writes may be captured into the Default update set (verify sys_update_xml and move rows with SN-Move-Records-To-Update-Set), GlideUpdateSet calls in it cannot change the update set other tools or the UI use (use SN-Set-Update-Set), and no rollback context is recorded. As a fallback it polls syslog for a correlation marker and reports "completed", "failed", or "timeout" (not a success); wait: false returns only trigger scheduling metadata immediately (see issue #40).

description.description: Why the script is being run (optional). Flattened to one line and appended to the script as a trailing comment, so it is recorded on the run's Script Execution History record.

instance.description: Configured ServiceNow instance name. Optional; uses the current instance when omitted.

record_for_rollback.description: Record a rollback context so the run's record changes can be reverted (default true). Applies to the /sys.scripts.do path only.

scope.description: Application scope to run in: an application sys_id, a scope name (e.g. "x_acme_app"), or "global" (optional; the processor default applies when omitted). Unknown scopes are rejected before anything runs. Only supported with wait: true; a non-global scope also rules out the sys_trigger fallback.

wait.description: If true (default), run through /sys.scripts.do and return the parsed result. If false, schedule a sys_trigger job and return immediately with only trigger scheduling metadata (fire-and-forget).
